remaining_delta: The problem is motivated by measured collaborative-prefix displacement inside GRAM fine item passages.
Each item is represented by a 64-token CF tensor and a 64-token metadata tensor whose total decoder capacity remains 128.
Both streams share the same historical item-position identity and use distinct field-source identities.
One textual-ID decoder is trained with paired full/CF-only/META-only gold-path non-degradation constraints.
strongest_counterargument: The method may still be an application of EAGER-style two-stream recommendation and established multimodal auxiliary-loss techniques; if factorization alone explains the effect or the non-degradation term adds no value, the method contribution is too thin.
required_rebuttal: J0-S must show that 64+64 simultaneously preserves collaborative identity coverage and improves important metadata coverage without increasing capacity.
Later experiments must include factorization-only and objective-only ablations.
The non-degradation objective must improve both recommendation metrics and paired source-interference metrics on a fresh dataset.
Compute, parameter and decoder-visible-capacity matching must be explicit.
search_limit: Bounded neighbor-cluster audit as of 2026-07-24; not proof of absolute novelty.
